seo_title: Cost of Living in Bali 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Bali per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: The region's main digital nomad hub: a warm climate year-round, well-developed infrastructure for remote workers and affordable villa rentals. Visa on arrival plus extension, card payments are limited.
pros: Developed infrastructure for remote workers — cafés, coworkings, fast Wi-Fi
Affordable villa rentals, especially outside Canggu and Ubud
A huge international digital nomad community
cons: Visa on Arrival is only for 30 days; you need an extension or a nomad visa
Lower healthcare quality — serious cases require evacuation to Singapore
Rainy season from November to March
Local bureaucracy for long-term living goes through agents
MIR cards don't work and taking money out is difficult

best_places.name: Canggu
best_places.description: The island's main nomad district: cafés, coworkings, beaches, bar-clubs.

best_places.name: Ubud
best_places.description: Jungle, rice terraces, a calm alternative to Canggu — for yoga and long-term work.

best_places.name: Outpost Ubud
best_places.description: The leader among the island's coworkings, networking every day and an on-site café.

best_places.name: La Brisa
best_places.description: A beach club in Canggu — the prime sunset spot with an Instagram-worthy vibe.

visa_steps.title: Visa on Arrival
visa_steps.description: 30 days on entry, payment $35 — for short trips and wintering.

visa_steps.title: VoA extension
visa_steps.description: Another 30 days through immigration or an agent — for 2,000–3,000 ₽.

visa_steps.title: B211A — socio-cultural visa
visa_steps.description: 60 days, extendable up to 180 — arranged through a sponsoring agent.

visa_steps.title: Digital Nomad Visa (E33G)
visa_steps.description: 5 years for remote workers earning from $60,000 — without the right to work for Indonesian clients.

visa_steps.title: KITAS
visa_steps.description: A work or retirement residence visa — for long-term stays and a local account.

faq.question: Can I work for a local company in Bali?
faq.answer: Without a KITAS it's a grey area. Many people do it, but there are risks during inspections.

faq.question: Where can I open an account in Bali?
faq.answer: Local banks require a KITAS. Without one — only e-wallets and foreign cards.

faq.question: How much does a visa agent cost in Bali?
faq.answer: From 3,000 to 10,000 ₽ for an extension, depending on the visa type and urgency.

faq.question: What is healthcare like in Bali?
faq.answer: Private clinics in Kuta and Denpasar — an appointment from 3,500 ₽. Serious cases — evacuation to Singapore.

faq.question: How much does it cost to rent a motorbike in Bali?
faq.answer: 70,000–100,000 IDR ≈ 400–600 ₽ a day. The nomads' main mode of transport.

faq.question: How do I pay in Bali?
faq.answer: Cash or a local card. MIR doesn't work. Many places are cash only.

reviews.text: Canggu is an alternative universe. I work in the morning, surf in the afternoon, and mix with an international community — a balance you won't find in Russia.
Bali is perfect for wintering. But living here permanently is hard: average healthcare, frightening bureaucracy, and sometimes you just want a normal city.
